row.team_price_text: Essential: $29/seat/mo (annual; a live price test also shows $19)
row.evidence: Intercom's pricing page lists "SSO & identity management" only under Expert ($132 per seat/mo) and says "The Expert plan supports SAML SSO ... SCIM provisioning works alongside SAML SSO"; the SCIM article requires SAML SSO, which "is only available on Expert Intercom plan."
row.notes: Status unchanged (gated, Expert). Prices unchanged from June in one page variant: Essential $29, Advanced $85, Expert $132 per seat/mo billed annually. The pricing page is A/B testing Essential: about half of 18 fetches on 2026-10-05 served $19 instead of $29 (Advanced and Expert identical), so the June $29 is kept and the conflict is recorded. The page's schema.org offers list monthly prices of $39/$99/$139. Fin AI Agent is billed separately at $0.99 per outcome. SCIM requires SAML SSO, which is Expert-only. Intercom has no deactivated state: SCIM deprovisioning (or active=false via Okta) permanently deletes the teammate from that workspace. REST API (Admins, Teams, Activity logs) is read-mostly: it cannot create, invite or remove teammates.

auth.token_source: Settings > Workspace > Security > Authentication methods > Provisioning > Enable SCIM provisioning (Base URL + API Token)
auth.notes: Docs call it an 'API Token' entered in the IdP's API integration; the header scheme is not spelled out, recorded as bearer per standard SCIM token use.

deprovision.data_retained: Teammate is permanently deleted from the workspace; their conversations, outbound messages, contacts and articles are reassigned per the Deprovisioning settings (default: first teammate in workspace). Access to other workspaces is retained.

attributes.notes: Only these attributes are mentioned; no full schema is published. Group attribute names are inferred from standard SCIM group push and are not listed by Intercom.

roles.how: Pushed IdP groups are mapped to Intercom roles, seat type and Copilot access in Settings > Workspace > Teammates > SCIM Provisioning; a default role cannot be set at provisioning time other than via group mapping.

limitations.text: No soft-deactivation: deprovisioning or deactivation in the IdP permanently deletes the teammate.
SCIM cannot add or remove a teammate from an Intercom team.
Limit of 100 SCIM groups per workspace and 2,500 users per SCIM group.
Each workspace must be a separate app in the IdP.
Okta requires the Application username format to be Email (userName must be an email).

endpoints.purpose: Retrieve a team and its admins

rate_limits.text: Private apps: 10,000 API calls/minute per app and 25,000 per workspace, distributed into 10-second windows.

limitations.text: The documented Admins API is read-only apart from away mode; there are no endpoints to create, invite or remove teammates.

okta.notes: OIN search card lists SAML, SWA and SCIM; Intercom's Okta guide configures SCIM through the catalogue app.

entra.notes: Intercom names Entra ID/Azure AD for SAML and SCIM token entry; no Microsoft Learn tutorial found at the usual URLs, so recorded as via_generic.

onelogin.notes: OneLogin store app 'Intercom SAML 2.0' per Intercom's own guide; OneLogin catalogue page not loaded. SCIM with OneLogin is mentioned only generically.

conflicts.text: The pricing page serves different variants: Essential shows $29 per seat/mo in some loads and $19 in others (annual toggle selected in both); card copy also varies. The page's schema.org offer data separately lists $39, $99 and $139 per seat/month (likely monthly billing).
The SCIM article says Intercom has no deactivated state and deletes the teammate, while the Okta guide lists 'Reactivate teammates' as supported.

open_questions: SCIM base URL pattern, supported filters, pagination and full attribute schema are not published.
Whether a deleted teammate's Full seat is released automatically is not stated.
Which plans include REST API access is not stated on the pricing page.
Whether a Microsoft Entra gallery app or Google/JumpCloud catalogue app exists is unconfirmed.
